title: improv·artist · vibratory (Ernesto Neto)
mutation_directive: improv artist: vibratory via Ernesto Neto

improv_extras.practice: stretched stocking sacs filled with spice; soft, droopy biomorphism

v1.feedback: Palette is genuinely excellent — cinnamon/nylon/turmeric/linen is exactly the aged earth-tone register this gallery rewards. The concept-to-code link is strong (Lucy classical form → Neto pendulous membrane). Two concerns: (1) the combined droop factor (2.8 multiplier) plus three simultaneous membrane wave components (frequencies 0.4–1.1) risk melting Lucy's silhouette into an unreadable sag — consider halving uDroop range and removing wave3 so the classical form stays recognizable through the deformation; (2) AdditiveBlending with a soft gaussian sprite (exp(-r*11.0)) on 60k particles will likely produce a hazy luminous cloud rather than the taut stocking-surface Neto actually achieves — try NormalBlending with a tighter falloff (exp(-r*22.0)) and slight opacity increase to get that translucent-fabric membrane read instead of additive glow.

v2.feedback: The Neto concept lands well — Lucy's silhouette is recognizable through the membrane droop and the spice-compartment color banding is a smart translation of his practice. The palette (cinnamon/turmeric/linen/nylon) is restrained and warm without crossing into oversaturation. Two refinements: the vibratory tremor amplitude (0.04–0.07 range) could be halved — at 60k particles the cumulative visual noise slightly erodes the silhouette legibility that makes this piece work, and the droop deformation pulls the lower torso into ambiguity. Consider making the droop height-dependent curve steeper so the head/shoulders stay crisp while only the lower hem sags, reinforcing the 'spice weight settling to the bottom of the stocking' read.
